name: Muḥammad
meaning: Muhammad (referring to the Prophet, pbuh) / Also known as Al-Qital (The Fighting).
revelation_details: Madinan (revealed early in the Madinan period).
core_theme: The nullification of the deeds of disbelievers versus the purification of believers, the characteristics of hypocrites, and the requirements for spiritual and physical victory.
name_origin:
The Surah is named after the mention of the Prophet (pbuh) in Verse 2:

• "And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition."*

The Alternative Name: Al-Qital

• Historical Context: Many scholars call this Surah Al-Qital because it contains the first detailed permissions and instructions regarding warfare after the migration to Madinah. It was revealed at a time when the Muslims were transitioning from a persecuted minority to a community that had to defend itself.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Eraser of Deeds vs. The Improver of States
verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: The Surah opens with a sharp contrast: those who disbelieve and bar others from the path of Allah will have their deeds rendered "void" or "lost." In contrast, those who believe, do righteous deeds, and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad - which is the Truth from their Lord - will have their sins removed and their "condition" (balahum) improved.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Faith is not just a mental state; it is a transformative power that repairs one's internal peace and external circumstances. Truth acts as a filter that validates or invalidates a person's life work.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: Allah addresses the reality of conflict between truth and falsehood. While Allah could have taken vengeance upon the disbelievers Himself, He tests believers through one another. Those killed in the cause of Allah will never have their deeds lost; He will guide them and admit them to the Paradise He has already made known to them. Allah promises that if you support His cause, He will support you and plant your feet firmly. He is the Protector of the believers, while the disbelievers have no protector.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: The struggle for justice is presented as a "test of sincerity" rather than a lack of God's power. Divine support is conditional upon the believer taking the first step toward standing for the Truth.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Rivers of Paradise vs. The Boiling of Hell
verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: A vivid comparison is drawn between the two destinations. Disbelievers enjoy themselves and eat like cattle, but the Fire is their home. In contrast, the Paradise promised to the righteous features four types of rivers: water that never goes stale, milk that never changes in taste, wine that is delicious to those who drink it, and purified honey. They will also have every kind of fruit and forgiveness from their Lord. This is contrasted with those who dwell eternally in Fire and are given boiling water that tears their intestines.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: The "cattle-like" existence of the disbeliever - living only for consumption - is contrasted with the sophisticated, sensory, and spiritual rewards of the believer.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Hypocrisy and the Pursuit of Knowledge
verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: Allah describes the hypocrites who sit and listen to the Prophet, only to ask mockingly afterward, "What did he just say?" Allah has sealed their hearts because they follow their own desires. For those who seek guidance, Allah increases them in it. The Surah reminds us that the "Hour" may come suddenly, and its signs have already appeared. The central command is: "Know that there is no god but Allah," and seek forgiveness for your sins and for the believers.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Guidance is a dynamic process; the more a person seeks it, the more God expands their capacity for it. Conversely, mockery and arrogance create a biological "seal" on the heart that prevents understanding.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: When a clear command for struggle is revealed, those with "disease in their hearts" look at the Prophet with the look of one fainting at the prospect of death. They promise obedience with their tongues but fail when the matter becomes serious. Allah warns that if they turn away, they may cause corruption on earth and sever family ties. Such people are cursed by Allah, who makes them deaf and blinds their vision. Allah asks: "Do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Sincerity is tested in times of hardship, not times of ease. The "locks" on the heart are often forged by a person's refusal to act on the knowledge they already possess.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Exposing the Secrets and the Test of Patience
verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: Allah tells the Prophet that the hatred in the hearts of the hypocrites will eventually be exposed. If Allah willed, He could show them to the Prophet so he would recognize them by their marks or the "tone of their speech." Allah promises to test the believers until the "mujahideen" (those who strive) and the "sabireen" (the patient) are clearly known and their records are made manifest.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Character cannot be hidden forever; it eventually leaks out through a person's words and reactions under pressure. The purpose of life's trials is to move "faith" from a claim to a proven reality.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Stewardship, Spending, and the Threat of Replacement
verse_breakdowns.content_markdown: The Surah concludes with a call to action: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not let your deeds go to waste." Believers are told not to be faint-hearted or call for peace out of weakness when they have the upper hand and Allah is with them. The life of this world is merely play and diversion. Allah asks for a portion of our wealth, not all of it. He warns that those who are stingy are only stingy toward themselves. Finally, a chilling warning: "If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: We are not doing God a favor by believing or spending; we are being given the honor of stewardship. If we fail to value the Truth, Allah will find others who will cherish it more than we did.

deep_dives.title: The Four Rivers of Paradise (Verse 15)
deep_dives.content:
One of the most unique and beautiful "descriptions" in the Qur'an is found in this Surah, detailing the environment of the Garden promised to the righteous.

The Divine Menu

Allah describes Paradise not just as a location, but through four specific types of rivers:

1. Rivers of Water: Unmodified in taste or smell (always fresh).
2. Rivers of Milk: The taste of which never changes (it never sours).
3. Rivers of Wine: Delicious to those who drink (it does not intoxicate or cause harm).
4. Rivers of Purified Honey.
• Tafsir Detail: Scholars note that these four liquids represent the primary needs and joys of the human palate, but in a perfected, eternal form that does not degrade.

deep_dives.title: The "Disease" of the Heart: Hypocrisy (Verses 20-30)
deep_dives.content:
This Surah provides a profound psychological analysis of the "hypocrites" (Munafiqun) - those who claimed faith but harbored doubt or cowardice.

• The Reaction to Revelation: Verse 20 describes how, when a clear Surah mentioning fighting was revealed, those with "disease in their hearts" would look at the Prophet with a "faint look of death."
• The "Locks" on the Heart: Verse 24 asks a rhetorical question: "Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?"
• The Recognition: Allah tells the Prophet that if He willed, He could point them out specifically, but he will recognize them anyway by the "tone of their speech" (v. 30). It teaches that hypocrisy eventually reveals itself through a person's words and attitudes toward sacrifice.

deep_dives.title: The Law of Divine Support (Verse 7)
deep_dives.content:
This Surah contains a foundational "equation" for success:

• "O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant your feet firmly."*

• Tafsir Context: "Supporting Allah" means supporting His religion, His Prophet, and the truth. It establishes that Divine help is conditional upon human effort and sincerity. If a person takes the first step toward the truth, Allah provides the "firmness" (Thabat) needed to endure.

deep_dives.title: The Warning of Replacement (Verse 38)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah ends with a powerful and sobering warning to the companions (and all Muslims):

• "And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you."*

• Historical Context: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (pbuh) was asked who these "other people" might be. In some narrations (Tirmidhi), he tapped the shoulder of Salman al-Farisi (who was Persian) and indicated that the Message would be carried by others if the Arabs failed in their duty.

Surah Muhammad serves as a manual for the sincere heart. It clarifies that faith is not just a feeling, but a commitment to the Truth that must be manifested through action and steadfastness in times of trial.
